indicator.subject: Science
indicator.content_standard: B5.1.1.2 Demonstrate understanding of the differences between living things, non-living things, and things which have never been alive
indicator.objective: Compare the differences among things that are living, dead and things that have never been alive

skills.description: Recognise that living things carry out life processes (growth, respiration, sensitivity, excretion, reproduction, nutrition).
Recognise that dead things were once alive but no longer carry out life processes.
Recognise that things which have never been alive do not and never did carry out life processes.
Classify examples as living, dead, or never alive (e.g. a growing plant, a dry stick, a rock).
Compare differences between living things and dead things (e.g. a living plant grows; a dead plant does not).
Give reasons for classifying something as living, dead, or never alive.

spec.difficultyPlan: 20 questions total — Difficulty 1: 5; Difficulty 2: 7; Difficulty 3: 5; Difficulty 4: 3.
misconceptions: A fire is living because it moves and grows.
A dead tree is not living, so it was never alive.
Water is living because it moves.
A car is living because it moves.
Things that move are always living.

questions.stem: What makes something a living thing?
options: It carries out life processes like growth and respiration
questions.explanation: Living things carry out life processes such as growth, respiration, sensitivity and excretion.
questions.misconception: Things that move are always living.

questions.stem: What does 'dead' mean?
options: Something that was once alive but no longer carries out life processes
hints: It was part of a tree but is no longer alive.
questions.explanation: Dead things were once alive but no longer carry out life processes.
questions.misconception: A dead tree was never alive.

questions.stem: What does 'never alive' mean?
options: Something that was never living and does not carry out life processes
questions.explanation: Things that have never been alive do not carry out life processes and never did.

questions.stem: Which of these is a living thing?
hints: Which one grows and carries out life processes?
questions.explanation: A growing plant is a living thing because it carries out life processes.
questions.misconception: Things that move are always living.

questions.stem: Which statement compares a living plant and a dead plant correctly?
options: The living plant grows, but the dead plant does not
The dead plant grows, but the living plant does not
hints: Dead things do not carry out life processes.
questions.explanation: A living plant grows, but a dead plant does not. This is one difference between living and dead things.

questions.stem: A pupil says a fire is living because it moves and grows. What is the best correction?
options: No, fire does not carry out life processes like respiration and excretion
questions.explanation: Fire is not living because it does not carry out life processes such as respiration and excretion.
questions.misconception: A fire is living because it moves and grows.

questions.stem: A pupil finds a dry leaf on the ground. How should the pupil classify it?
hints: It was once part of a living plant.
questions.explanation: The dry leaf was once part of a living plant but is no longer alive. It is dead.

questions.stem: Why is a rock classified as 'never alive'?
options: Because it does not carry out life processes and never did
questions.explanation: A rock is never-alive because it does not carry out life processes and never did.

questions.stem: Which of these is a difference between a living thing and a dead thing?
options: Living things move, but dead things do not
Living things carry out life processes, but dead things do not
Living things are always bigger than dead things
hints: Living things carry out life processes.
questions.explanation: Living things carry out life processes, while dead things do not. This is a key difference.
questions.misconception: Dead things still carry out life processes.

questions.stem: Which of these was never alive?
hints: Was it ever part of a living thing?
questions.explanation: A rock was never alive. Dry sticks, dead insects and fallen leaves were once part of living things.

questions.stem: What makes something a living thing?
answer: it carries out life processes like growth and respiration
it grows and breathes
it carries out life processes
hints: Living things carry out life processes.
questions.explanation: A living thing carries out life processes such as growth, respiration, sensitivity and excretion.

questions.stem: What does it mean when something is dead?
answer: it was once alive but no longer carries out life processes
it was once living but is no longer alive
it was alive but is not now
questions.explanation: Dead things were once alive but no longer carry out life processes.
questions.misconception: A dead thing was never alive.

questions.stem: A pupil classifies a car as 'never alive'. Which reason is correct?
options: It moves, so it is living
It does not carry out life processes and was never alive
It is made of metal, so it is dead
It has wheels, so it is living
questions.explanation: A car is never-alive because it does not carry out life processes and was never alive.
questions.misconception: A car is living because it moves.

questions.stem: Which statement correctly compares living and dead things?
options: Living things grow and respire, but dead things do not
Dead things grow, but living things do not
Both living and dead things respire
Neither living nor dead things grow
hints: Living things carry out life processes.
questions.explanation: Living things grow and respire, but dead things do not carry out life processes.

questions.stem: Classify a rock as living, dead, or never alive.
answer: never alive
never alive because it was never living
hints: It does not carry out life processes.
questions.explanation: A rock is never alive because it does not carry out life processes and never did.

questions.stem: Give one reason why a dry stick is classified as dead.
answer: it was once part of a living tree but no longer carries out life processes
it was once alive but is no longer alive
it was part of a living plant but is now dead
hints: Was it ever part of a living thing?
questions.explanation: A dry stick was once part of a living tree but no longer carries out life processes, so it is dead.

questions.stem: What does 'never alive' mean?
answer: something that was never living and does not carry out life processes
something that was never alive
it was never living
questions.explanation: Never alive means something was never living and does not carry out life processes.

questions.stem: A pupil has four things: a growing bean plant, a dry leaf, a stone, and a dead insect. Which list correctly classifies them?
options: Living: growing bean plant; Dead: dry leaf and dead insect; Never alive: stone
Living: growing bean plant and dry leaf; Dead: stone; Never alive: dead insect
Living: stone; Dead: growing bean plant; Never alive: dry leaf and dead insect
Living: dead insect; Dead: growing bean plant; Never alive: stone and dry leaf
hints: Which ones were once alive but are not now?
questions.explanation: The growing bean plant is living. The dry leaf and dead insect were once alive but are now dead. The stone was never alive.

questions.stem: Explain one difference between a living plant and a dead plant.
answer: a living plant grows and carries out life processes, but a dead plant does not
the living plant grows, but the dead plant does not
living plants respire, dead plants do not
questions.explanation: A living plant grows and carries out life processes, while a dead plant does not.

questions.stem: Explain why a car is not a living thing, even though it moves.
answer: because it does not carry out life processes like growth and respiration
it moves but it does not grow or breathe, so it is not living
a car is never alive because it does not carry out life processes
questions.explanation: A car is not living because it does not carry out life processes such as growth and respiration, even though it moves.
questions.misconception: Things that move are always living.
